context.requirement_text:
Closes the layering and restart-intensity portions of ISS-0425/GH#829
(queue task 425), sized per ISSUE-FIXER's own diagnosis
(handoffs/WF03-ISS0425-20260903/step-01-issue-fixer-diagnosis.json):
Letflow.Application.start/2 (lib/letflow/application.ex:26-139, read
2026-09-03) builds ONE flat list of 20 children -- Letflow.Repo,
Ecto.Migrator, Oidcc.ProviderConfiguration.Worker, Letflow.Registry,
Letflow.Metrics.Registry, Letflow.Admission (REQ-216),
Letflow.InstanceSupervisor, 7 Task.Supervisors (SandboxPool, Plugin,
Lua, Wasm.ModuleRegistry, Wasm.CapabilityGate,
Wasm.ModuleVersionRegistry, Obs.Alerts), Letflow.SandboxPool,
Letflow.Engine.PluginRegistry, Letflow.Engine.Wasm.ModuleVersionRegistry,
Letflow.Scheduler.Poller (REQ-186, gated :start_scheduler),
Letflow.Engine.ServiceTaskDispatcher.Poller (REQ-214, gated
:start_service_task_dispatcher), and Bandit (gated :start_http) -- all
as peers under one `Supervisor.start_link(children, strategy:
:one_for_one, name: Letflow.Supervisor)` with no
max_restarts/max_seconds override (OTP default: 3 restarts/5s).
DOCUMENTED, NON-HYPOTHETICAL INCIDENT THIS REQUIREMENT MUST MAKE
STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: scheduler_children/0's own comment
(application.ex:154-172) and ISS-0421 both describe a Poller whose
zero-delay first tick (`Process.send_after(self(), :tick, 0)`) raises
DBConnection.OwnershipError repeatedly under Ecto sandbox mode until
the shared top-level supervisor's restart intensity is exceeded and
the WHOLE application -- Letflow.Repo and Bandit included -- shuts
down. REQ-214's ServiceTaskDispatcher.Poller (application.ex:181-197)
documents the IDENTICAL hazard for a second, independent poller. Both
are currently worked around only by disabling them under test
(config/test.exs), not by any structural isolation -- a real
production crash-loop in either poller still takes the whole node
down today.
DECISIONS (settled here, not left to CODE-DESIGNER, per this
project's own REQ-216/217/218 design-gate precedent of resolving
real open questions at the requirement stage):
1. TOP-LEVEL SHAPE: three new sibling supervisor modules under
lib/letflow/supervisor/ -- Letflow.Supervisor.Infrastructure,
Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, Letflow.Supervisor.Http (each `use
Supervisor`, own start_link/1 and init/1) -- become the ONLY 3
children of Letflow.Application's own Supervisor.start_link/2 call,
under strategy: :one_for_one (NOT :rest_for_one, deliberately
diverging from ISS-0425's own "candidate shape" text: ISSUE-FIXER's
diagnosis names the concrete reason -- :rest_for_one at the top would
cascade-restart every LATER-listed layer whenever an EARLIER one's
supervisor exits, e.g. a rare Infrastructure exit would force-restart
Pollers AND Http even though neither holds a pid-based dependency on
any Infrastructure child, since every named-process infra child
(Repo, both Registries, all 7 Task.Supervisors, InstanceSupervisor)
is looked up BY NAME at each call site, never by stored pid).
:one_for_one at the top means a Pollers crash-loop exhausting ITS OWN
restart intensity kills and restarts ONLY Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers
-- Infrastructure (Repo included) and Http are never touched. This is
the structural fix for the documented incident above.
2. LAYER MEMBERSHIP (every one of the 20 current children assigned):
Letflow.Supervisor.Infrastructure owns, in EXACTLY their current
relative order (preserving both hand-maintained ordering constraints
below as a property of Supervisor's own sequential per-child startup,
not a comment): Letflow.Repo, Ecto.Migrator,
Oidcc.ProviderConfiguration.Worker, Letflow.Registry,
Letflow.Metrics.Registry, Letflow.Admission, Letflow.InstanceSupervisor,
SandboxPool.TaskSupervisor, Letflow.SandboxPool,
Engine.PluginTaskSupervisor, Engine.PluginRegistry,
Engine.Lua.TaskSupervisor, Engine.Wasm.ModuleRegistryTaskSupervisor,
Engine.Wasm.CapabilityGateTaskSupervisor,
Engine.Wasm.ModuleVersionRegistry,
Engine.Wasm.ModuleVersionRegistryTaskSupervisor,
Obs.Alerts.TaskSupervisor -- strategy: :one_for_one, OTP default
restart intensity (crash-looping infra, e.g. Repo itself, indicates a
fault severe enough that taking the whole app down is still the
correct behavior; this requirement does not change that). Letflow.
Supervisor.Pollers owns Letflow.Scheduler.Poller and
Letflow.Engine.ServiceTaskDispatcher.Poller (each still individually
gated by its own existing :start_scheduler /
:start_service_task_dispatcher config key -- an empty children list
when both are false, as under config/test.exs today, must start and
run without error). Letflow.Supervisor.Http owns Bandit (still gated
by :start_http).
3. RESTART INTENSITY PER LAYER: Letflow.Supervisor.Infrastructure and
Letflow.Supervisor.Http keep the OTP default (3 restarts/5s) -- no
documented incident motivates changing either. Letflow.
Supervisor.Pollers gets an EXPLICIT override, looser than the OTP
default to tolerate a handful of transient per-tick failures (a
single bad HTTP dispatch, a single locked row) without exiting:
max_restarts: 5, max_seconds: 60, recorded with this rationale in the
module's own moduledoc. Whichever value is chosen, the requirement's
AC4 below is the real bar -- a sustained crash-loop must still
exceed it and cause Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers (only) to exit and be
restarted once by the top-level Letflow.Supervisor.
4. ORDERING CONSTRAINTS PRESERVED (verified in application.ex as of
2026-09-03, both currently comment-enforced only): (a) ISS-0224 --
SandboxPool.TaskSupervisor before {Letflow.SandboxPool, []}, within
Letflow.Supervisor.Infrastructure's own list, unchanged relative
order; (b) ISS-0429 -- Obs.Alerts.TaskSupervisor before either
Poller's first tick can reach it, now structural: Letflow.
Supervisor.Infrastructure completes its ENTIRE startup (Supervisor's
own guarantee: each child's init/1 returns before the next child
starts) before Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers starts at all, which is a
strictly stronger guarantee than list-position-within-one-flat-list.
SEQUENCING NOTE FOR ISS-0421: ISS-0421 (Scheduler.Poller SPOF, 7
serial per-tenant sweeps) is explicitly waiting on this requirement
to settle restart-intensity policy before it decides its own,
narrower, Poller-internal fix (per both issues' own text: "whichever
runs second reads the other's outcome"). This requirement's decision
3 above (Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers: max_restarts 5, max_seconds 60)
is that settled input; ISS-0421's own fix must build on it, not
re-decide a conflicting intensity policy.
NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT, AND WHY:
(a) ISS-0421's own internal Poller fix (bounding the 7 serial
per-tenant sweeps, e.g. via Task.async_stream) -- separate, narrower,
sequenced to land after this requirement per both issues' own text.
(b) ISS-0422's CLAUDE.md/requirements.yaml wording drift -- confirmed
documentation-only and unrelated; not touched here.
(c) The Task.Supervisor sprawl review (ISS-0425 part 3) -- REQ-220.
(d) Reversing REQ-045's row-based-instance decision, or giving
Letflow.InstanceSupervisor real children -- ISS-0425's own text is
explicit this is NOT in scope. InstanceSupervisor is placed inside
Letflow.Supervisor.Infrastructure alongside the other currently-inert
leaf children, matching its CURRENT behavior (an empty
DynamicSupervisor); this is not a claim about which layer it belongs
in once (if ever) a future requirement gives it real children -- left
as an explicitly open question for that future requirement, not
guessed at here.
